prompt.adult: The LORD promises to take His people from among the nations. According to Ezekiel 36:24, from where will He gather them, before He brings them into their own land?
prompt.child: God promised to bring His people home. After taking them from among the nations, from where did He say He would gather them?
prompt.teen: Ezekiel 36:24: “gather you out of” what, “and bring you into your own land”?
prompt.older: According to Ezekiel 36:24, out of what will the LORD gather them?

verses.text: For I will take you from among the nations, gather you out of all countries, and bring you into your own land.

explanation.child: Look right after “gather you out of” in verse 24.
explanation.teen: 36:24 has three movements: take, gather, and bring. Read the middle one.
explanation.older: It follows “gather you out of” in 36:24.

teaching.extended_explanation: 36:24 also says He will take them from among the nations and bring them into their own land.
teaching.takeaway: He will gather them out of all countries.

prompt.adult: John 16:10 speaks of righteousness, because Jesus goes to the Father. In 16:12 He says He still has many things to say to them, but they are not able to do what now?
prompt.child: Jesus told His disciples He still had many things to say. What did He say they were not able to do now?
prompt.teen: John 16:12: what does He say they are not able to do now?
prompt.older: Read with 16:10, what does 16:12 say they are not able to do now?

verses.text: of righteousness, because I go to My Father and you see Me no more;
“I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 12.
explanation.teen: 16:10 speaks of His going; 16:12 ends with what they are not able to do now. Read the end.
explanation.older: It is the last phrase of 16:12.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:12 also says, “I still have many things to say to you.” 16:10 says, “you see Me no more.”
teaching.takeaway: They were not able to bear them now.

verses.text: Nevertheless I tell you the truth. It is to your advantage that I go away; for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you; but if I depart, I will send Him to you.
of sin, because they do not believe in Me;

prompt.adult: Acts 2:16 says this is what was spoken by Joel. In 2:1, when the Day of Pentecost had fully come, how does the verse describe where they were?

with one accord in one place

prompt.adult: Romans 8:25 speaks of hoping for what we do not see. In 8:24, after “For we were saved in this hope,” what does Paul say hope that is seen is not?
prompt.child: Paul writes about the hope in which believers were saved. What does he say hope is not, if it is already seen?
prompt.teen: Romans 8:24: “For we were saved in this hope, but” what?
prompt.older: Read with 8:25, what does 8:24 say hope that is seen is not?

choices.text: hope that is seen is not hope
hope that is seen is not peace
hope that is seen is not sure
hope that is seen is not proof

verses.text: For we were saved in this hope, but hope that is seen is not hope; for why does one still hope for what he sees?
But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly wait for it with perseverance.

explanation.child: Look right after “is not” in verse 24.
explanation.teen: 8:25 speaks of waiting; 8:24 defines hope that is seen. Read that word.

teaching.extended_explanation: 8:24 also asks, “for why does one still hope for what he sees?” 8:25 says, “we eagerly wait for it with perseverance.”
teaching.takeaway: Hope that is seen is not hope.
